newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa stumbles to new lows on spec selling.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa stumbles to new lows on spec selling.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures tumbled Thursday, hitting fresh contract lows across the board, as heavy speculative selling continued to batter the market, floor sources said.

Most-active March cocoa plunged to a new life-of-contract low of $1,259 a tonne before settling at $1,260, down $30 on the day. On the continuous weekly chart, today's finish was the lowest in 10 months.
Second-month May slid $26 to $1,295, while the back months closed $18 to $33 lower. Volume was heavy at an estimated 16,277 lots.

"It is partically currency-related," said Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka. "And there is a lot of cocoa around. Cocoa is acting as if it is seeing more cocoa available than the numbers are showing."

While of arrivals out of Ivory Coast lagged behind last year's, the pace appeared to pick up recently. Ivorian industry sources pegged arrivals by Jan 20 at around 710,000 to 720,000 tonnes compared with 765,000 a year ago. A crop of more than one million tonnes was likely, they said. Last season produced a record 1.2 million tonnes.
Traders said the dollar's continued strength against Sterling pressured the New York market from the outset, as arbitrage sold dollar-denominated CSCE futures.
March futures breached key technical support at $1,280, activating sell stops and accelerating the slide, they added.
Technically, traders said March should find strong support at $1,250.

But after posting four consecutive sessions of losses, and dropping $65 -- or about five percent -- in the past two sessions alone, traders and analysts said the market was due for a technical correction. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk 212 859 1640))
